title: fix(plugin-security): count and warn the derived capability skip that leaves the platform bucket unseeded
body:
Fixes #8536

**Observability only.** The #5876 guard keeps declining an authored row — that is the ruled behaviour, and #8552 settled the posture on an occupied platform bucket: keep declining, loudly, with no adoption and no backfill. Nothing about what the seeder writes changes here; what changes is whether an operator can tell what it declined to write.

## The premise, measured before implementing

Verified on `origin/main`, not assumed. The new headline pin was run against the unmodified source first: every assertion before the new counter **passed**, which is the premise —

- the guard fires (`skippedAuthored === 1`),
- the organization's row is untouched,
- `platformRowFor(ql, 'showcase.export_data')` is `undefined` — the platform bucket really is left empty,
- `seeded` does not move.

And it was silent: `bootstrap-system-capabilities.ts` had exactly one `logger?.warn?.` call site, inside the curated branch. So the silent skip is still silent, and the card's premise stands.

## Why the silence became wrong

The derived lookup is `{ name }` and runs under `SYSTEM_CTX`, which carries no `tenantId`, so it reads **across organizations** by construction. Before #8461 that was harmless because `name` was unique installation-wide: "a row resolves this name" and "the platform holds a row for this name" were **one statement** — which is exactly what #5876's reasoning rests on ("the capability resolves and the authored copy is the better one").

Per-organization uniqueness (ADR-0120 D1) separated those two statements. An organization's row now satisfies the lookup while the NULL-organization bucket is never written at all, and `continue` runs **before any insert is attempted** — so unlike the curated half there is not even a swallowed refusal to observe. Nothing anywhere reported the empty bucket.

## Which counter carries it — the judgement, stated

Three options were on the table; the code decided it.

- **Reuse `skippedAuthored`.** Rejected: that counter cannot distinguish "an authored copy was left alone" (benign, the thing #4632 declined to alarm about) from "the platform's definition exists nowhere". Reusing it would bake in exactly the conflation #8461 created.
- **Split it in two.** Rejected: it changes the meaning and the value of a field already returned in `CapabilitySeedResult` and logged in the boot summary, for no gain — the two facts are both worth reporting.
- **Additive subset — chosen.** `skippedAuthored` keeps its meaning and its value (every skip, as before); the new `unseededDerived` counts the documented **subset** whose skip leaves the platform bucket with no platform-owned row. Neither fact is inferred from the other.

`unseededDerived` is the derived counterpart of `blockedCurated` — same harm, different route.

## The warning means exactly one thing

The skip branch reads the platform bucket **once, on that branch only** — the same cost the curated half already accepted — because the row just skipped says nothing about the platform's own bucket. It may be an organization's row while the bucket sits empty, the bucket's own occupant, or neither: the platform's placeholder may be present and simply not have been the row the lookup selected. Those are different facts, so the seeder reads rather than infers.

It warns only where the platform's own placeholder is genuinely **absent**. A skip that declines a mere *refresh* stays summary-only, which is what keeps the warning meaningful instead of firing on every authored row.

The message follows the curated half's rule of naming what it **read**, never asserting an ownership verdict: the blocking row's `managed_by` and organization, plus which of three bucket observations was seen (free / held by an unstamped row / held by a row with a named provenance). The #8552 hand-resolution line prints only where a row an operator may legitimately rename is what blocks the bucket; where an organization's row is what stands in the way, the message says there is nothing to remove — that row is a supported ADR-0066 D1 extension ("admins EXTEND the registry"), and telling an operator to delete it would be bad advice.

## Pins — discrimination, not just "it fires"

Seven new tests. Both directions:

- an organization row blocks the derivation: warns, counts, names the real `managed_by` **and** the real organization id (`org_jia_9f2` — deliberately distinctive, so a placeholder cannot pass), states the bucket is free, and does **not** print the hand-resolution line;
- a provenance matrix over `admin` / `package` / absent, each asserting the value named is the one read and that the *other* row's provenance never appears;
- the platform bucket held by an authored row: warns, and here the hand-resolution line **does** print;
- **opposite-direction control 1** — an ordinary derivation: bucket free, capability seeded, no warn, counter does not move;
- **opposite-direction control 2** — the sharp one: the guard fires and `skippedAuthored` moves, but the platform placeholder **exists**, so nothing is reported.

Behaviour-unchanged assertions ride along in each: the org row is compared with `toEqual`, the bucket is still empty afterwards, `seeded` does not move.

**Ablation, run and restored from the commit:** replacing the "placeholder exists" early-continue with an unconditional warn turns control 2 red (`expected 1 to be +0`) and **only** control 2 — 30 of 31 still pass. So the control has teeth and the warn is genuinely conditional. A test-fixture bug surfaced the same way and was fixed rather than papered over: a helper parameter defaulted to `'admin'` silently rebuilt the absent-`managed_by` row as an admin row, because a JS default fires on an explicitly passed `undefined`; the default is gone and every call site now states its provenance.

## Verification

Union re-run **after** the final commit, at `HEAD` = `40610b3` — the merge commit that synced with `main`. The sync moved `main` under the branch, so the whole union (build closure, tests, typecheck, every gate below) was re-run at that head rather than reported from the pre-merge run: a ratchet measured against different code is a stale claim, and `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` is exactly that kind of gate.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` — 60 files, **1146 passed** (1139 before this change; +7 new)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` — clean
- Gates re-derived from the actual diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, which surfaced five changeset-family gates the dispatch list did not name (it was derived on the source surface only): `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-empty-changeset.mjs`. All run, all green, together with `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:i18n`, `check:type-check-coverage` and `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` (the last on a built workspace closure).

Scope held to `bootstrap-system-capabilities.ts` + its test, plus the changeset. `packages/metadata-protocol` untouched. Synced with `main`; PR #8713's surface (`src/security-plugin.ts`, `permission-set-active.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/**`) is disjoint.
